items.title: Finite triangulations of compact PL surfaces

items.statement: A **finite triangulation of a compact PL surface** is a finite two-dimensional simplicial complex $K$ in which each edge is incident to one or two triangles and the link of each vertex is homeomorphic to a circle or a closed interval. Its realization $|K|$ is the surface; its boundary is the subcomplex formed by edges incident to one triangle and their vertices. If $V,E,F$ are the numbers of vertices, edges and triangles, its simplicial Euler characteristic is $\chi(K)=V-E+F$.

items.title: Choice-free homology and longitude computation for a supplied knot tube
items.statement: Let $K:S^1\to S^3$ be a smooth oriented embedding and suppose a product tubular embedding $\Phi:S^1\times D^2_{2\epsilon}\to S^3$ is supplied, where $D^2_r=\{z\in\mathbb R^2:|z|\le r\}$. Define $N=\Phi(S^1\times D^2_\epsilon)$, $E=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N$, $T=\partial E$, and let $i:T\hookrightarrow E$ be inclusion. Fix $s_0\in S^1$ and $z_0\in\partial D^2_\epsilon$. Let $\mu=\Phi(\{s_0\}\times\partial D^2_\epsilon)$ be the fibre meridian and let $\sigma:S^1\to T$ be the product section $s\mapsto\Phi(s,z_0)$. Then $H_1(E;\mathbb Z)$ is infinite cyclic generated by $i_*[\mu]$. The kernel of $i_*:H_1(T;\mathbb Z)\to H_1(E;\mathbb Z)$ has a unique generator $[\lambda]$ whose image under the product projection $H_1(T;\mathbb Z)\to H_1(S^1;\mathbb Z)$ is $1$, and $([\mu],[\lambda])$ is a basis of $H_1(T;\mathbb Z)$. The proof uses no choice axiom beyond the supplied tube.

items.title: Essential simple curves on a torus are primitive
items.statement: Let $T=S^1\times S^1$ be the standard oriented product torus. If $C\subset T$ is an embedded piecewise-linear simple closed curve that is not null-homotopic, then its class $[C]\in H_1(T;\mathbb Z)$ is nonzero and primitive, meaning that it is not $k x$ for any $x\in H_1(T;\mathbb Z)$ and integer $|k|>1$.

items.statement:
Assume countable choice. Let a compact embedded surface in a smooth three-manifold have a supplied finite whole-star piecewise smooth triangulation: its simplex maps extend smoothly, and their differential fan is injective on the entire tangent star at every point. Suppose its boundary has an already smooth embedded collar in the surface. Then the surface can be replaced, in any prescribed neighborhood and fixed on a smaller boundary collar, by a smooth embedded surface homeomorphic to it relative to that collar. The replacement can also be fixed on any specified compact subset on a neighborhood of which the surface is already smooth. In particular an embedded disk with such data and smooth boundary collar has a smooth embedded disk replacement with exactly the same boundary.

A finite PL surface in the compatible PL structure of a supplied whole-star smooth triangulation of the ambient manifold has the required piecewise smooth data after common subdivision. This clause concerns compatibility with the specified smooth triangulation; it does not assert compatibility of an arbitrary topological marking.

items.title: Smooth proper disks have PL approximations in a compatible triangulation

items.statement: Assume countable choice. Suppose a compact smooth three-manifold $M$ with boundary has a supplied finite compatible whole-star smooth triangulation, with boundary a subcomplex and differential fans homeomorphic onto the boundary tangent half-spaces. If $M$ contains a smooth properly embedded disk transverse to its boundary, it contains a properly embedded PL disk whose boundary is isotopic in $\partial M$ to the original boundary. In particular essentiality of the boundary is preserved. PL here refers to the supplied compatible structure; no arbitrary topological triangulation is substituted.

items.title: Closed PL surfaces with even original-edge counts separate
items.statement: Let $M$ be a connected compact PL three-manifold with a finite simplicial triangulation $T$. Let $S\subset\operatorname{int}M$ be a connected closed locally flat PL surface. Suppose $S$ misses the original vertices, is transverse to the original edges, and meets every original global edge in an even number of points. Then $M\setminus S$ is disconnected. Neither $M$ nor $S$ is assumed orientable, and no irreducibility or choice principle is required.

items.statement: Let $n\ge1$, and let $A$ be an integer matrix with at most $n$ rows and at most $n$ columns, all entries in $\{-1,0,1\}$. Deterministic algorithms compute its rational rank and an independent set of original rows in time polynomial in $n$ and sequential Turing workspace $O(n^2\log(n+2))$ bits. The determinant of any specified square submatrix is computable within the same bounds. If $A$ has $b\ge1$ columns and rational rank $b-1$, a primitive integer generator of its one-dimensional rational kernel is computable within those bounds, with either choice of its overall sign. The zero-row and zero-column matrices and the $0\times0$ determinant convention are included.

items.title: Matching equations and finite bounds for normal coordinates
items.statement: Let $T$ be a finite tetrahedral triangulation of a compact piecewise-linear $3$-manifold with $t\ge1$ tetrahedra. A nonzero nonnegative integer vector in $\mathbb Z^{7t}$ is the normal-coordinate vector of a normal surface exactly when it satisfies every face-matching equation and at most one quadrilateral type is nonzero in each tetrahedron. Every primitive integer generator of an extreme ray of the Haken cone has each coordinate at most $2^{7t-1}$. Every fundamental normal-surface vector has each coordinate at most $t\,2^{7t+2}$.

items.statement: Let $E$ be the compact exterior of a smooth knot with supplied product boundary torus $T=S^1\times S^1$, fibre meridian $\mu$, and unique degree-one zero-homology longitude class $[\lambda]$ from the product data. Let $D\subset E$ be a properly embedded piecewise-linear disk, meaning an embedded copy of the closed disk with $D\cap T=\partial D$. If $\partial D$ is not null-homotopic in $T$, then $[\partial D]=[\lambda]$ or $-[\lambda]$ in $H_1(T;\mathbb Z)$, and its mod-two intersection number with $\mu$ is $1$.

references.title: Joel Hass, Jeffrey C. Lagarias and Nicholas Pippenger, The Computational Complexity of Knot and Link Problems
references.locator: §4, peripheral coordinates and the disk criterion; the curve-straightening and capping annulus are constructed locally.

items.statement: Assume countable choice. In a supplied smooth product solid torus $S^1\times D^2$, let $C\subset S^1\times\partial D^2$ be a finite PL, or finite piecewise smooth regular, embedded simple closed curve. Interpret PL in the compatible structure of the smooth product. If the projection $C\to S^1$ has degree $1$ or $-1$, then $C$ and the core $S^1\times\{0\}$ cobound an embedded annulus in the solid torus. The annulus is finite piecewise smooth, smooth on a neighborhood of its core boundary, has its other boundary exactly $C$, and otherwise lies in the interior of the solid torus. Consequently it may be glued to any properly embedded exterior disk with boundary $C$ to give an embedded disk with boundary the smooth core and a smooth collar there.

items.title: Essential PL disks admit normal disk replacements

items.statement: Let $M$ be a compact PL three-manifold with a finite simplicial triangulation. If $M$ contains a properly embedded PL disk whose boundary is not null-homotopic in $\partial M$, then it contains a normal disk with that property. No orientability, irreducibility or projective-plane hypothesis is required. The construction is allowed to replace disk pieces and to change the isotopy class of the original disk; it asserts existence of a normal replacement.

items.title: Compatible normal disk boundary paths have a unique type-preserving switch
items.statement:
Let $P,Q$ be two normal disk types in one tetrahedron, subject to quadrilateral compatibility. Thus if both are quadrilaterals they have the same type. Choose two distinct faces $f,g$ met by both types, and cut each normal boundary word at one point of its arc in $f$ and one point of its arc in $g$. Each boundary is divided into two paths from $f$ to $g$.

There are two pairings that join one path from $P$ to one from $Q$ at both ends, producing two new closed boundary words. Exactly one pairing gives the original two normal disk boundary types, as an unordered pair, up to cyclic rotation and reversal of the words. The other pairing has a word crossing some tetrahedral edge at least twice and therefore cannot give those two normal types.

The conclusion concerns the finite boundary words and type counts in the original tetrahedron. It does not assert that arbitrary surface intersections already have the geometric regular-position or partial-switching properties.

items.title: Triangular normal arcs admit braid position stable under partial regular switches

references.title: Wolfgang Haken, Theorie der Normalflächen, Acta Mathematica105 (1961),245–375
references.locator: Chapter4, Hilfssatz8 and Hauptsatz4, braid pieces and regular switches. The central-triangle and three-strip construction below is given directly inside an original triangular face.

items.statement:
Let $f$ be an affine triangle and let $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ be two finite families of normal arcs in $f$, each family embedded and pairwise disjoint, with disjoint endpoint sets on $\partial f$. There are PL representatives of the same individual arc types, fixing those endpoints, with these properties:

1. Every intersection is a transverse double point between the two families. Each original pair of arcs intersects at most once.
2. At every double point there is a chosen regular reconnection. For every subset of the double points, perform just those reconnections and otherwise retain the original transverse crossings. The resulting parametrizing components are embedded normal arcs, never circles, and their total counts of the three normal arc types are unchanged. Every remaining double point lies on two distinct parametrizing arcs.
3. The chosen reconnection at a crossing is the unique one of the two uncrossings that preserves the unordered pair of the two normal arc types there. Its alternative creates an edge-return arc in that local two-arc endpoint pairing. The same characterization holds at each remaining crossing after any partial reconnection.

Here parametrizing components follow the strands through unswitched crossings without joining them. The construction uses a small central triangle and three quadrilateral strips inside this original face. It changes no triangulation and uses only finite choices.

items.title: A regular normal-sum diagram has a reduced connected pair

references.title: Wolfgang Haken, Theorie der Normalflächen, Acta Mathematica105 (1961),245–375
references.locator: Chapter5§1, printed pp.361–364, definition of reduced normal pairs, the separation consequence, and complete proof of Satz7. The finite maximal-switch argument is expanded below with its input interface explicit.

items.statement:
Let $T$ be a finite simplicial triangulation of a compact PL three-manifold. Suppose a **regular normal-sum diagram** is supplied with the following data:

- Two nonempty embedded normal surfaces $X,Y$ in transverse PL position, with no triple points and finitely many disjoint double circles and proper double arcs.
- Pairwise disjoint switching neighborhoods of those double curves, disjoint from $T^{(1)}$, with compatible chosen regular switches. In each tetrahedron the local switch reconnects two crossing normal disks to normal disks of the same two types. A partial switch therefore leaves a finite immersed normal-disk diagram, with only the unswitched double curves and without branch points. Switches in disjoint neighborhoods commute.
- Performing all the switches gives a connected embedded normal surface $F$.

Then some partial switching gives a diagram whose normalization has exactly two components $G,H$. Here normalization means separating the two branches at every remaining double point; its components are the parametrizing surfaces, regardless of intersections between their images. Both $G$ and $H$ are connected embedded normal surfaces. They have

$$v(G)+v(H)=v(F),\qquad w(G)+w(H)=w(F),\qquad 0<w(G),w(H)<w(F).$$

Their remaining switching system is reduced in the following precise sense: switching any nonempty subset of its curves gives a diagram with connected normalization. In particular no remaining intersection circle or proper intersection arc separates both $G$ and $H$ when each is cut along its corresponding preimage.

All surfaces and vectors remain in the original triangulation $T$. No orientability, irreducibility or choice hypothesis is needed. The existence of a regular normal-sum diagram from an arbitrary coordinate decomposition is an input to this lemma, not a conclusion.

items.title: Normal exchange disk patches have positive edge weight

references.title: Chan-Ho Suh, The Unknotting Problem and Normal Surface Q-Theory
references.locator: §2.5, exchange surfaces and disk patches; §3.3, the least-weight disk-patch construction.

items.statement:
Let $T$ be a finite simplicial triangulation of a compact PL three-manifold $M$, and let $F$ be a normal surface. Its normal disks form polygonal cells with three or four sides. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite disjoint family of PL simple closed curves and properly embedded PL arcs on $F$. Suppose $\Lambda$ misses the normal-cell vertices, is transverse to the cell edges, and meets each normal disk in disjoint properly embedded arcs whose endpoints are on distinct sides of that disk.

Cut $F$ along $\Lambda$, retaining separate boundary copies of each cut. Let $P$ be the compact completion of one resulting component, and suppose $P\cap\partial F$ has $b$ components, all proper arcs. Define its edge weight by $w(P)=|P\cap T^{(1)}|$. If $w(P)=0$, its polygonal pieces have $k_j\ge2$ trace sides and satisfy

$$\chi(P)=\frac b2+\sum_j\left(1-\frac{k_j}{2}\right)\le\frac b2.$$

Consequently, if $P$ is a disk and $b\le1$, then $w(P)>0$. This applies in particular to disk patches of a proper normal sum: an interior disk patch has one closed trace frontier and $b=0$, and a boundary disk patch has one trace-arc frontier and $b=1$.

The trace hypothesis is satisfied by the usual exchange rectangles: in each tetrahedron a rectangle has two opposite sides on distinct normal disks and the other two sides in distinct tetrahedral faces. No orientability, irreducibility or projective-plane hypothesis is imposed.

items.title: Admissible normal vectors have rigid averages of tetrahedral edge counts

references.title: Joel Hass, Jeffrey C. Lagarias and Nicholas Pippenger, The Computational Complexity of Knot and Link Problems
references.locator: §5, the seven tetrahedral disk types. The edge-count kernel and admissible averaging statement are proved directly below.

items.statement:
For a finite tetrahedral triangulation, let $B$ record the six local edge-intersection counts in every tetrahedron from its seven normal coordinates. Let $u,v,d$ be nonnegative real normal-coordinate arrays, each using at most one quadrilateral type in each tetrahedron. They need not satisfy matching equations. If $\alpha,\beta>0$ and

$$\alpha Bu+\beta Bv=(\alpha+\beta)Bd,$$

then

$$\alpha u+\beta v=(\alpha+\beta)d.$$

In particular, if $u,v,d$ are actual normal-surface vectors, the hypothesis may be checked on their global triangulation-edge intersection counts. If those counts for $u$ and $v$ average to those for $d$, then their normal-coordinate vectors also average to $d$.

If $d$ is lexicographically least in any set of vectors containing $u,v,d$, this averaging identity forces $u=v=d$. Thus two essential normal disks of the same least edge weight whose edge counts average to those of a lexicographically least such disk must have exactly that disk's normal vector.

items.title: Finite normal-coordinate tests characterize essential disk candidates
items.statement: Let $E$ be a triangulated compact exterior of a smooth knot with peripheral torus $T$ and a marked simple fibre meridian $\mu$ in the boundary triangulation. For an admissible normal-coordinate vector $v$ and its associated normal surface $S$, the following tests hold exactly when $S$ is a connected properly embedded disk with non-null-homotopic boundary in $T$: (i) $S$ is connected; (ii) $\partial S\ne\varnothing$; (iii) $\chi(S)=1$; and (iv) $\partial S$ has odd mod-two intersection with $\mu$. If $v$ is fundamental, connectedness follows from fundamentalness.

items.title: Smooth-to-piecewise-linear knot exterior approximation
items.statement: Assume countable choice. Let $K:S^1\to S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with a supplied product tubular embedding $\Phi:S^1\times D^2_{2\epsilon}\to S^3$. There is a polygonal knot $P$ inside this tube and a smooth rounding $K'$ of $P$ such that $K'$ is smoothly ambient isotopic to $K$ by an isotopy supported in the tube. If $K$ is supplied with a finite regular projection diagram $D$, the polygonal approximation and rounding can be chosen to have the same crossing code as $D$. A homeomorphism supported in the larger tube carries $P$ to $K'$, preserves the boundary torus of the radius-$\epsilon$ tube, and sends each marked fibre meridian to itself up to orientation. Conversely, every polygonal knot $P$ with a finite product regular neighborhood can be rounded in pairwise disjoint vertex balls to a smooth knot $P^\sharp$; a homeomorphism supported in those balls carries its compact exterior and marked meridian to those of $P^\sharp$. If a regular projection diagram is supplied, the rounding balls can be chosen away from crossing charts, so the crossing code is unchanged. These clauses compare smooth knot type through smooth knots and polygonal exterior models through homeomorphisms; they do not treat a nonsmooth polygonal curve as a smooth isotopy slice.

items.title: Positive-Euler finite PL surfaces are disks, spheres or projective planes

references.title: Wolfgang Haken, Theorie der Normalflächen, Acta Mathematica105 (1961),245–375
references.locator: Chapter5, printed pp.360–374, positive-Euler summands in the fundamental-surface argument. The small finite surface classification used here is proved below.

items.statement:
Let $P$ be a connected compact surface supplied with a finite PL triangulation. The following conclusions require no choice axiom.

1. If $\partial P\ne\varnothing$, then $\chi(P)\le1$. Equality holds only for a disk. If instead $\chi(P)=0$, then $P$ is an annulus or a Mobius band; these have respectively two and one boundary circles.
2. If $\partial P=\varnothing$, then $\chi(P)\le2$. If $\chi(P)=2$, then $P$ is a two-sphere; if $\chi(P)=1$, then $P$ is a projective plane.

Consequently, every positive-Euler connected finite PL surface is a disk, sphere or projective plane. These identifications can be made by PL homeomorphisms between finite polygonal models. In a PL three-manifold without an embedded projective plane, a connected embedded positive-Euler surface is therefore a disk or a sphere.

items.title: Zero-edge normal exchange rectangles and annuli have cellwise product structures
items.statement:
Let $F$ be a normal surface in a finite simplicial triangulation $T$. Cut $F$ along a finite disjoint trace family satisfying the distinct-normal-side hypothesis of the positive patch-weight lemma, and let $R$ be a connected compact cut patch missing $T^{(1)}$.

If $R$ is a disk with two trace-arc boundary sides and two original-boundary arc sides, then its normal-cell regions form a finite chain of quadrilaterals. The opposite trace arcs are parallel by a PL product parametrization of $R$: every intermediate arc meets each region of this chain in one arc joining its two old sides, and its endpoints stay within the two original boundary sides. These old sides lie in distinct tetrahedral faces.

If $R$ is an annulus whose two boundary components are trace circles and which misses $\partial F$, its normal-cell regions form a finite cycle of quadrilaterals. There is a PL product parametrization by $S^1\times[0,1]$ taking its two trace circles to the two end levels and keeping each intervening arc within its original normal-cell region. A Mobius patch instead has the twisted interval-bundle model and does not have two trace boundary components.

The parallelisms take place on the cut patch, cell by cell in the original triangulation. No ambient three-dimensional product region or cancellation of a separate exchange surface is asserted.

items.title: Polynomial verification of a primitive normal vertex-disk certificate
items.statement: Let $T$ be a good triangulation of a knot exterior with $t$ tetrahedra and a marked meridian path in its triangulated boundary torus. A certificate consists of a nonnegative integer vector $v$ with $7t$ binary-encoded coordinates, a set of active matching and zero-coordinate constraints, a nonzero $(7t-1)$-minor witnessing their rank, and the marked boundary data. A deterministic verifier can check the certificate in time polynomial in the certificate bit length. Acceptance verifies that $v$ is a primitive admissible extreme-ray vector of the Haken cone and that its associated normal surface is a properly embedded disk with non-null-homotopic boundary. The verifier uses arithmetic on the compressed coordinates and does not expand the normal surface into its potentially exponentially many normal disks.

items.title: Compatible normal vectors admit regular sum diagrams in the original triangulation

references.title: Wolfgang Haken, Theorie der Normalflächen, Acta Mathematica105 (1961),245–375
references.locator: Chapter4 Hauptsatz4, printed pp.356–360, compatibility of partial regular switches. No identification of its adapted coordinates with the original seven coordinates is assumed here.

items.statement:
Let $T$ be a finite simplicial triangulation of a compact PL three-manifold. Let $x,y\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{7t}$ be admissible normal-coordinate vectors such that $x+y$ satisfies the quadrilateral condition. There are embedded proper normal surfaces $X,Y$ with vectors $x,y$, a finite transverse double-curve diagram $X\cup Y$ disjoint from $T^{(1)}$, and pairwise disjoint switching neighborhoods with these properties:

1. In each tetrahedron all double arcs join distinct faces. At every such arc the chosen regular switch preserves the unordered pair of normal disk types.
2. The choices agree through every crossed face and hence along each entire double circle or proper double arc.
3. Any partial selection of whole-curve regular switches gives a finite immersed normal-disk diagram with only the unswitched double curves and no branch points. Its total vector is $x+y$. Switches in disjoint neighborhoods commute.
4. Switching all curves gives an embedded proper normal surface $F$ with $v(F)=x+y$ and $w(F)=w(X)+w(Y)$.

The realization of an admissible vector determines its abstract surface and its boundary curves up to PL homeomorphism of the surface and homotopy of the corresponding boundary curves in $\partial M$. In particular, if $x+y=v(D)$ for a connected essential normal disk $D$, then $F$ is a connected essential normal disk. Thus every nontrivial coordinate decomposition of such a disk has an actual regular normal-sum diagram of this kind in the original triangulation.

No irreducibility, orientability, sphere-separation or choice hypothesis is required. The assertion concerns these explicitly constructed realizations, without claiming an ambient isotopy between arbitrary prior realizations.

items.title: Irregular switches in original face braids strictly improve essential disks

references.title: Wolfgang Haken, Theorie der Normalflächen, Acta Mathematica105 (1961),245–375
references.locator: Hauptsatz4 and Satz8, printed pp.356–366, irregular-switch fold and strict normalization. The proof below supplies the fold on an original triangulation edge by a first-turnback argument in the actual face braid, rather than transferring the adapted F-number.

items.statement:
Start with the normal diagram constructed by the original-triangulation regular-sum construction, retaining its central-triangle and three-strip face braids. Let $W=w(X)+w(Y)$. A preliminary subset of its double curves may already have been switched regularly.

On some of its remaining double curves choose either the regular switch or its opposite, called an **irregular switch**, leaving the others unswitched. Suppose at least one irregular switch is performed. If a parametrizing component $P$ of the resulting diagram has an embedded proper PL disk as its image and its boundary is essential in $\partial M$, then there is an essential normal disk $D'$ in the original triangulation with

$$w(D')<W.$$

Other components may intersect the image of $P$ along unswitched double curves; only $P$ itself is required to be embedded. Parametrizing components separate the branches at unswitched crossings. No irreducibility, orientability, projective-plane or choice hypothesis is imposed.

items.title: An embedded projective plane meets the one-skeleton of a finite three-triangulation
items.statement:
Let $T$ be a finite simplicial triangulation of a compact PL three-manifold $M$. Every PL embedded projective plane in $\operatorname{Int}M$ meets $T^{(1)}$. The manifold may be nonorientable and may contain projective planes. No irreducibility or choice hypothesis is imposed.

More precisely, every compact subset of $\operatorname{Int}M\setminus T^{(1)}$ lies in the interior of an explicitly parametrized finite thickening of the dual graph, built from convex three-ball vertex pieces and standard disk-prism edge pieces. An embedded projective plane in such a thickening would lift into a parametrized finite tree of these balls, contradicting its nonorientability.

items.title: A nonvertex fundamental disk has a connected two-copy normal sum
items.statement:
Let $D$ be a fundamental normal disk in a finite simplicial triangulation $T$. If its vector $d$ does not lie on an extreme ray of $C(T)$, there are connected embedded normal surfaces $X,Y$, neither with vector proportional to $d$, and an actual original-triangulation regular diagram whose full resolution has vector

$$v(X)+v(Y)=2d.$$

Its full resolution consists of two disks with boundary curves homotopic to $\partial D$. Exactly one of the following occurs:

1. $X$ and $Y$ are disks.
2. One is a sphere and the other is an annulus; both annulus boundary curves are homotopic to $\partial D$.

If $D$ is in addition a least-weight essential normal disk with lexicographically least vector at that weight, the first case has at least one disk with null-homotopic boundary. This is a reduction of the vertex obligation, not a proof that either case is impossible.

items.title: Between-copy annular exchange caps have rigid original edge counts
items.statement:
Let $D$ be an essential normal disk of least original-edge weight and, among such disks, of lexicographically least normal vector in a finite simplicial PL three-manifold triangulation. In an actual original-triangulation regular normal diagram, suppose two distinct full-resolution components $D_0,D_1$ have vector $d=v(D)$. Let one of its exchange annuli $A$ have one frontier circle on each of these components, with its usual rectangular switching neighborhood and interior disjoint from the full resolution.

Let $E_i\subset D_i$ be the disk cap bounded by that circle. Then $N(E_0)=N(E_1)$ on every original global edge and $w(E_0)=w(E_1)>0$. Replacing either cap by the other cap joined across $A$ gives an embedded proper essential PL disk with the original boundary of that copy. Each replacement has edge-count vector $N(D)$, and every componentwise edge-nonincreasing essential normal replacement of it has vector $d$.

No irreducibility, orientability or fundamentalness assumption is required. Equal edge counts here do not assert that the caps are normally parallel or that the exchange lies in the product between the two copies.

items.title: Meridian-disk criterion for unknot recognition
items.statement: Assume countable choice. Let $K:S^1\to S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with a supplied product tubular neighborhood, and let $E_K$ be its compact exterior with peripheral torus $T_K$, fibre meridian $\mu$, and the unique degree-one generator $[\lambda]$ of the kernel of $H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)\to H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$ supplied by the product-tube Mayer–Vietoris calculation. Then $K$ is ambient isotopic in the smooth category to the standard unknot if and only if $E_K$ contains a properly embedded piecewise-linear disk $D$ whose boundary is not null-homotopic in $T_K$. Every such disk has $[\partial D]=[\lambda]$ or $-[\lambda]$ and has odd mod-two intersection with the original marked meridian $\mu$.

items.title: Closed normal subdiagrams inherit strict irregular disk improvement

references.title: Wolfgang Haken, Theorie der Normalflächen, Acta Mathematica105 (1961),245–375
references.locator: Hauptsatz4 and Satz8, printed pp.356–366. The restriction to actual original-triangulation parametrizing components and its own edge weight is proved below.

items.statement:
Take an actual original-triangulation regular normal diagram, retaining its face braids after any preliminary whole-curve regular switches. Choose a nonempty union $S$ of whole components of its parametrizing normalization. Assume every remaining double curve incident to $S$ has both branches in $S$. Retain its geometric strands, tetrahedral disk pieces and remaining double curves, and write $W_S$ for the total number of its original edge-intersection points, counted on those parametrizing components.

Resolve any selection of these remaining curves regularly or irregularly. If at least one irregular switch is made, and the resulting normalization has a component whose image is an embedded proper disk with essential boundary in $\partial M$, then the original triangulation contains an essential normal disk of weight strictly less than $W_S$.

The chosen $S$ may be a single immersed parametrizing component with self-double curves; no partition of it into two globally embedded normal families is assumed. The closure condition concerns the actual remaining double curves, not merely a selection of tetrahedral disk types.

items.title: Smooth knots have compatible piecewise-linear exterior models
items.statement: Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot with a finite regular projection diagram $D$ having $n$ crossings and a supplied product tube. There is a polygonal knot $P$ inside that tube with the same crossing code as $D$ and a smooth rounding $K^\sharp$ of $P$ such that $K^\sharp$ is smoothly ambient isotopic to $K$. The compact exterior of this same $P$ has a good triangulation with at most $C(n+1)$ tetrahedra and a marked path for the original meridian with at most $C(n+1)$ boundary edges, for one universal constant $C$. The peripheral-preserving exterior homeomorphism transfers this model to $K^\sharp$.

items.title: Haken–Jaco–Tollefson normal-surface unknot search
items.statement:
**Input:** A finite tagged Gauss code, signed Dowker–Thistlethwaite code, or oriented planar-diagram code in the code conventions of the planar-code definition, and a mode, either **Haken** or **JT**.

**Output:** The first validation error with its witness; **not-a-knot** for a valid code with more than one component; **disk-certificate** with a normal-coordinate vector and its finite witness data; or **no-candidate** after the selected search is exhausted.

**Procedure:**

1. Run the planar-code validation procedure. Return its first invalid result if validation fails. If the validated code represents more than one component, return **not-a-knot**.
2. Let $n$ be its crossing count. Construct the good triangulated exterior $E$ with $t\le C(n+1)$ tetrahedra and the marked original meridian path.
3. In Haken mode, enumerate all vectors $v\in\mathbb Z^{7t}$ with $0\le v_i\le t2^{7t+2}$ in lexicographic order. Retain a vector only if it satisfies all matching equations and quadrilateral restrictions and is fundamental. Fundamentalness supplies connectedness. Compute nonempty-boundary, Euler-characteristic, and mod-two meridian-intersection data from the compressed coordinates, without expanding the surface. Return **disk-certificate** at the first vector passing these tests; return **no-candidate** after the finite box is exhausted.
4. In JT mode, let $A$ be the integer matching matrix and put $m=7t$. Enumerate all subsets $Z\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}$ in lexicographic order. For each $Z$, append the equations $v_i=0$ for $i\in Z$ to $Av=0$. If the combined matrix has rank $m-1$ and its one-dimensional kernel contains a nonzero nonnegative vector, compute the unique relatively prime nonnegative integer generator $v$ of that ray. Require that its positive-coordinate support be exactly the complement of $Z$; this visits each ray once, at its exact zero-coordinate support. Discard vectors that violate the quadrilateral restriction. A primitive generator on an extreme ray is fundamental, so its surface is connected. Compute nonempty-boundary, Euler-characteristic, and mod-two meridian-intersection data from the compressed coordinates, without expanding the surface. Return **disk-certificate** at the first passing vector; return **no-candidate** after all subsets have been processed.

The candidate tests use the boundary arcs and Euler-characteristic data computed from the compressed normal coordinates. No correctness or complexity assertion is part of this algorithm definition.

items.title: A nonfundamental least-weight essential disk has a pure boundary obstruction
items.statement:
Let $F$ be a least-edge-weight essential normal disk in a compact PL three-manifold with a finite simplicial triangulation $T$. If its normal vector has a nontrivial admissible decomposition, construct the original-triangulation regular diagram and a reduced connected pair $P,H$ using the original-triangulation regular-sum construction and the reduced-connected-pair lemma. Retain their face braids and switch neighborhoods.

After interchanging the two summands if necessary, $P$ is a disk with null-homotopic boundary in $\partial M$, and $H$ is an annulus or a Mobius band. Their intersection consists of $k\ge2$ properly embedded arcs and no circles. Every intersection arc separates $P$ and does not separate $H$. Cutting all the arcs leaves $k+1$ disk patches in $P$ and $k$ disk patches in $H$.

There are at least two patches $E$ of $P$ with exactly one cut-arc side and one original-boundary side. Each has positive edge weight. Choose such a patch of smallest weight. Boundary compression of $H$ along $E$ produces an embedded proper PL disk $D_E$ satisfying

$$w(D_E)=w(H)+2w(E)\le w(H)+w(P)=w(F).$$

If $\partial D_E$ is not null-homotopic in $\partial M$, then every inequality displayed above is an equality, and normal replacement of $D_E$ can retain an essential disk only at weight $w(F)$. The lemma makes no assertion that this boundary is essential. No irreducibility, orientability or exclusion of projective planes is assumed.

items.title: Same-copy exchanges on least fundamental disks have disjoint adjacent caps

references.title: Chan-Ho Suh, The unknotting problem and normal surface Q-theory
references.locator: Theorem3.12 preliminary annular and proper-arc cases. The proof below instead uses fundamentalness and the original retained-diagram irregular improvement, so does not assume irreducibility or annular patch positivity.

items.statement:
Let an actual original-triangulation regular normal diagram have full embedded resolution $F$. Suppose a component $D$ of $F$ is an essential normal disk, is fundamental, and has least weight among all essential normal disks in that triangulation.

Choose one original double circle or proper double arc whose two trace curves in the full resolution both lie on $D$. Assume its exchange surface is respectively an annulus or a disk with its usual rectangular switching neighborhood. Then the traces bound disjoint adjacent disk caps on $D$. For a proper exchange disk these are the two outer caps cut off by the two trace arcs. For an exchange annulus the unique two caps bounded by the trace circles are disjoint and adjacent.

Here adjacency means that the two cap germs occupy the same side of the exchange surface in its switching neighborhood. The result concerns these actual original-diagram exchanges, not an arbitrary separately supplied spanning annulus. No irreducibility, orientability or sphere-separation assumption is required.

items.title: Between-copy proper exchanges have essential diagonals and rigid cap counts
items.statement:
Let $D$ be a least-weight essential normal disk in a finite simplicial triangulation of a compact PL three-manifold, with lexicographically least normal vector among essential disks at that weight; put $d=v(D)$. In an actual original-triangulation regular diagram whose full resolution consists of two disjoint disks $D_0,D_1$ with vector $d$, choose an original proper double arc whose exchange disk joins a trace on $D_0$ to a trace on $D_1$.

Switch every other original curve regularly and leave this arc unswitched. Its two affected parametrizing components are embedded essential normal disks, each with vector $d$. In the transverse exchange rectangle choose the cap on the upper side at each frontier, denoting these adjacent caps by $E_0,E_1$; write $K_i$ for the complementary disk in $D_i$. Then

$$N(E_0)=N(E_1)>0,\qquad N(K_0)=N(K_1)>0,$$

where equality is componentwise on the original global edges and positivity means positive total weight. The two original diagonal disks are $E_0$ joined to $K_1$ and $K_0$ joined to $E_1$, along their original exchange continuations. The opposite, irregular pairing gives two embedded proper PL disks, at least one with null-homotopic boundary. This holds without fundamentalness, irreducibility, orientability or a choice principle. No normal parallelism of the caps is asserted.

references.title: Horst Schubert, Bestimmung der Primfaktorzerlegung von Verkettungen, Mathematische Zeitschrift76 (1961),116–148
references.locator: §5.4, second case, printed pp.139–141, the uncut disk and opposite disk construction. The boundary essentiality and original-edge equality below are proved directly.

items.statement:
Choose a least-edge-weight essential normal disk $F$ whose normal vector is lexicographically least among such disks. Suppose a nontrivial vector decomposition has been put into the retained original-triangulation regular diagram and reduced to the pair $P,H$ of the pure boundary-obstruction lemma. Thus $P$ is a disk, $H$ is an annulus or Mobius band, and their remaining intersections are $k\ge2$ proper arcs.

Let $E$ be a leaf disk patch of $P$, with sole cut-arc side $\alpha$. Regularly switch every remaining double arc except $\alpha$, and cut the two parametrizing copies of $\alpha$. There are exactly three disk pieces: $E$, an opposite end disk $E'$, and a middle disk $K$. Their images have pairwise disjoint interiors; their only coincident boundary arcs are the indicated copies of $\alpha$. The irregular switch along $\alpha$ joins $E$ to $E'$ into an embedded proper disk $W$. Its boundary is null-homotopic in $\partial M$.

Replacing either end disk by a second parallel copy of the other produces embedded proper disks

$$A=K+2E,\qquad A'=K+2E'.$$

Both have essential boundary. For every original edge $e$ of $T$,

$$|E\cap e|=|E'\cap e|.$$

Both disks have weight $w(F)$, and their essential normal replacements have exactly $F$'s normal vector and preserve every original edge count. These conclusions do not assert that $E,E'$ are normally isotopic or that their intervening region can be cancelled.

items.title: Actual same-copy exchange caps have rigid original edge counts

references.title: Chan-Ho Suh, The unknotting problem and normal surface Q-theory
references.locator: Theorem3.12 cap replacement. The componentwise original-edge equality and full lexicographic conclusion are proved below without irreducibility.

items.statement:
In an actual original-triangulation regular diagram let a full-resolution component $D$ be a fundamental essential normal disk, of least weight among essential normal disks and with lexicographically least normal vector at that weight. Let an annular or proper disk exchange belonging to this diagram have both trace components on $D$.

Its disjoint adjacent disk caps $E,E'$ have equal counts on every original triangulation edge and positive total edge weight: $N(E)=N(E')$ and $w(E)=w(E')>0$. Replacing either cap by a nearby copy of the other along the exchange gives an embedded proper PL disk with essential boundary. Both replacements have edge-count vector $N(D)$, and their componentwise edge-nonincreasing normal replacements have exactly the original normal vector $v(D)$.

For a proper disk exchange, the alternative disk obtained by joining its two outer caps along the exchange has null-homotopic boundary in $\partial M$. No assertion of normal parallelism of $E,E'$ is made.

items.title: Minimum boundary exchange leaves have a single-leaf zero-edge corridor
items.statement:
Use the least-weight and lexicographically least disk $F$, reduced boundary pair $P,H$, and leaf/opposite-cap construction of the leaf-cap rigidity lemma. Choose a leaf disk patch $E$ of $P$ with smallest weight among all such leaves, and let $E'$ be its opposite end disk.

View these pieces on the regular full-resolution disk $F$, retaining the two traces of every exchange arc and the exchange rectangle off $F$ between them. Then $E'$ contains exactly one original leaf disk patch $L$ of $P$, with its small half-switch-band collars included. It has $w(L)=w(E)>0$. Either $E'=L$, or the closure of $E'\setminus L$ is a disk corridor with two trace-arc sides, two original-boundary sides, and zero edge weight. In the latter case its original normal-cell product structure gives an isotopy of the cap $E'$ onto $L$ on $F$, fixing its original edge intersections and keeping every point in its original normal cell. This is a finite cap transport on the given normal disk; it asserts no ambient three-dimensional filling or cancellation of a cycle of exchanges.

items.title: Boundary exchange middle disks have positive original edge weight
items.statement:
In the leaf/opposite-cap construction of the leaf-cap rigidity lemma, write the regular disk as $F=E+K+E'$, where $E,E'$ are its two end disks and $K$ is the middle disk. Then $w(K)>0$. In particular

$$w(F)>2w(E)=2w(E').$$

This holds without excluding projective planes from the ambient manifold. The one-skeleton and all switches are those of the original triangulation.

items.title: Equal normal vectors have ambient cell homeomorphisms and disk-copy products
items.statement:
Two embedded normal surfaces with the same normal vector in a finite simplicial triangulation are carried to one another by a finite PL homeomorphism of the ambient manifold preserving every simplex setwise.

Consequently, if $D_0,D_1$ are disjoint connected normal disks with the same vector, they cobound a parametrized PL product $D^2\times[0,1]$. Its two end disks are $D_0,D_1$, its vertical boundary is in $\partial M$, and it contains no original triangulation vertex. Its interval fibers remain in their original ambient simplex. The assertion concerns the supplied PL triangulation, not an arbitrary topological marking or a smooth extension problem.

items.title: Exchange surfaces inside normal disk-copy products are vertical
items.statement:
Let $P$ be a supplied cellwise normal product between disjoint equal-vector connected normal disks $D_0,D_1$ in a finite simplicial three-manifold triangulation. Thus each tetrahedral part of $P$ is a parametrized disk prism between corresponding normal disk pieces, each face part is the corresponding normal-arc strip, and the product fibers stay in their original ambient simplex.

Suppose an embedded exchange annulus or proper exchange disk $A$ lies in $P$, misses the original one-skeleton, and spans $D_0,D_1$. More explicitly, its two frontier components are respectively a circle or proper arc on each end disk; it meets each tetrahedral prism in disjoint proper rectangles, each with one frontier arc on each horizontal end, joining the same two distinct original faces at both ends; its remaining sides are the face arcs of $A$. In the disk case its remaining boundary is in the vertical boundary of $P$ in $\partial M$.

The product parametrization can be chosen to make $A$ vertical, while its fibers still remain in their original ambient simplex. In the annulus case the two disk caps bounded by its frontier cobound a normal product with vertical boundary $A$. In the disk case both pairs of corresponding disk caps cut off by its frontier arcs cobound such products, with the other vertical boundary strips in $\partial M$. In particular these caps are normally parallel along $A$.

items.title: Least-weight lexicographic essential normal disks are fundamental
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a compact PL three-manifold with a finite simplicial triangulation $T$. Among its essential normal disks choose one of least edge weight, and among those choose $F$ with lexicographically least normal vector. Then $F$ is fundamental in the original seven-coordinate system of $T$.

Consequently, if $M$ contains a properly embedded PL disk whose boundary is not null-homotopic in $\partial M$, it contains such a disk that is a fundamental normal surface. No ambient orientability, irreducibility or exclusion of projective planes is required, and no choice hypothesis is introduced.

items.title: Original between-copy exchanges contained in normal products are vertical
items.statement:
Let $F$ be the full resolution of an actual original-triangulation regular normal diagram. Let two distinct disk components $D_0,D_1$ bound a supplied cellwise normal disk product $P$: its tetrahedral pieces are the disk prisms between corresponding normal pieces, its face pieces are their normal-arc strips, and its fibers stay in their original simplices.

Let $A$ be an exchange annulus or proper exchange disk of that diagram, with one frontier component on each $D_i$, with its usual rectangular switching neighborhood. Suppose $A\subset P$. Then the product can be parametrized to make $A$ vertical while preserving its simplex incidence. In the annular case its two disk caps are normally parallel along $A$. In the disk case both corresponding cap pairs are normally parallel along $A$, with their remaining vertical boundary in $\partial M$.

This concerns the actual original-diagram exchange surface inside the supplied cellwise product. It makes no assertion that an arbitrary between-copy exchange is contained in that product, or can be moved there by following first contact.

items.title: Between-copy annular exchanges on least disks have adjacent caps
items.statement:
Use the least-weight, lexicographically least essential disk $D$, distinct full-resolution copies $D_0,D_1$, actual annular exchange $A$, and disk caps $E_0,E_1$ of the between-copy annular cap-rigidity lemma. Supply a cellwise normal product $P$ between $D_0,D_1$, with vertical boundary in $\partial M$.

Then $E_0,E_1$ are adjacent along $A$: their germs occupy the same side of its rectangular switching neighborhood. This holds without irreducibility or orientability. It does not assert normal parallelism of these caps when $A$ lies outside $P$.

items.title: Reduced sphere-annulus sums cannot realize two least fundamental disks
items.statement:
Let $D$ be a fundamental essential normal disk in a finite simplicial triangulation of a compact PL three-manifold. Suppose $D$ has least edge weight among all essential normal disks, and lexicographically least normal vector among those of that weight; put $d=v(D)$.

There is no actual original-triangulation regular-sum diagram $X\cup Y$ of the following reduced kind. The surfaces $X,Y$ are respectively a connected normal sphere and a connected normal annulus, their vectors are not proportional to $d$, and $v(X)+v(Y)=2d$. All partial regular resolutions retain normal tetrahedral disk pieces, and the full resolution consists of two copies $D_0,D_1$ of $D$. The number of original double circles is least among diagrams of this kind, including diagrams obtained by regularly switching a subset when the two resulting families remain an embedded sphere and annulus.

No irreducibility, orientability or choice hypothesis is required. The conclusion excludes this sphere-annulus branch only; it does not exclude a sum of two disk summands.

items.title: Reduced two-disk sums of least fundamental disks have no closed exchanges
items.statement:
Let $D$ be a least-weight essential fundamental normal disk with lexicographically least vector at that weight, in a finite simplicial triangulation of a compact PL three-manifold; put $d=v(D)$. Let $X,Y$ be connected embedded normal disks with neither vector proportional to $d$ and $v(X)+v(Y)=2d$.

Suppose an actual original-triangulation regular-sum diagram for them has full resolution $D_0\cup D_1$, the two disk copies of $D$, and retains genuine normal tetrahedral disk pieces under every partial regular resolution. Choose it with the smallest number of double curves among eligible two-disk diagrams, including those obtained by a partial regular switch when its resulting disk families are embedded and nonproportional to $d$.

Then every original double curve is a proper arc. At least one of $\partial X,\partial Y$ is null-homotopic in $\partial M$. The conclusion does not exclude those remaining proper exchanges, and assumes neither orientability nor irreducibility nor a choice principle.

items.title: Least-weight lexicographic essential normal disks are vertex disks
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a compact PL three-manifold with a finite simplicial triangulation $T$. Among its essential normal disks choose $D$ of least original edge weight and lexicographically least normal vector at that weight. Then $d=v(D)$ is primitive and lies on an extreme ray of the full Haken matching cone $C(T)$ in the original seven coordinates per tetrahedron.

Consequently, if $M$ contains a properly embedded PL disk whose boundary is not null-homotopic in $\partial M$, it contains such a primitive vertex normal disk in the same triangulation. No orientability, irreducibility, sphere-separation, projective-plane exclusion or choice hypothesis is required.

items.title: Correctness and finite bounds of the Jaco–Tollefson vertex search
items.statement: For a valid one-component knot code, the JT primitive extreme-ray search accepts if and only if the triangulated exterior contains a properly embedded disk with non-null-homotopic boundary. It examines at most $2^{7t}$ support subsets for a $t$-tetrahedron exterior, each candidate coordinate has $O(t)$ bits, and its sequential Turing space is $O(t^2\log(t+2))$ bits.

items.title: Unknot recognition has a polynomial-bit normal-surface certificate
items.statement: Assume countable choice. For a valid finite $n$-crossing one-component knot code $D$, let $T_D$ be the fixed deterministic good exterior triangulation with $t\le C(n+1)$ tetrahedra and the marked original meridian path, recomputed from $D$ by the stated finite construction. The smooth knot represented by $D$ is the unknot if and only if it has a certificate consisting of a nonnegative $7t$-coordinate normal vector $v$, active matching and zero-coordinate constraints, and a nonzero $(7t-1)$-minor witnessing their rank, all relative to $T_D$. A deterministic verifier reconstructs $T_D$ and its meridian path from $D$ and checks the certificate in time polynomial in its bit length, without expanding the represented normal surface.

items.title: Termination, correctness, and bounds of normal-surface unknot recognition
items.statement: Assume countable choice. For every valid one-component knot code with $n$ crossings, both the Haken and JT normal-surface searches terminate and decide whether the smooth knot represented by the code is ambient isotopic to the standard unknot. The Haken search uses $2^{O(n^2)}$ Turing time and $O(n^2\log(n+2))$ Turing space. The JT primitive-vertex search uses $2^{O(n)}$ Turing time and the same space bound. The zero-crossing case is handled by a fixed finite construction. No polynomial-time claim is made.
